text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout started for rl-v3 (ratecap/exemptions change) at 2026-03-15T10:02:36Z — canary: eu-west-1, 5% traffic
priya: seeing 429 spikes in hosted-prod dashboards right after the canary start, alerting on high 429 rate for /v1/generate
maya: paging oncall — I'm oncall now, investigating. Maya here.
jordan: I rolled the change that reconciles exemption lists for token accounting — it landed in canary at 10:02Z. My first guess is mismatch in exemption mapping logic.
maya: can you paste the deploy id or flag?
jordan: deploy id: deploy/rlv3-exemptions/2026-03-15-1001. Feature flag: `rlv3_exemptions_v2=true` (canary).
ashley: logs show a surge of `quota_exceeded` errors from the rlv2 -> rlv3 routing path, sample: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T10:03:01Z","svc":"ratecap","err":"quota_exceeded","account":"acct-9a3","tokens_needed":120,"tokens_alloc":0}
```
priya: affected tenants seem mostly dedicated and some hosted enterprise — reprod curl against token endpoint shows missing exemptions for accounts that should be grandfathered.
maya: can we kill the flag quickly? What are rollback options: feature flag flip vs deploy rollback?
jordan: safest fast path is flip the flag to false for canary region. Config service accepts a single API call: ```bash
curl -X POST https://config.prod.redwood/api/flags/rlv3_exemptions_v2 -d '{"value":false,"target":"eu-west-1"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
ashley: I prefer rollback of canary slice in orchestrator to avoid partial state; but flag flip is lower blast radius and immediate.
maya: flipping flag now, will monitor metrics. Doing it via `configctl` so it's auditable.
maya: `configctl set rlv3_exemptions_v2 --region eu-west-1 false`
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation triggered (PD#INC-33421) — severity: P1. Oncall: maya. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/INC-33421
devin: support queue is lighting up. Support has 12 open tickets referencing 429s in last 10m. I'll start templated customer update.
support-lead: target list: 6 dedicated tenants + 3 enterprise customers showing sustained 429s. Prioritize dedicated.
ashley: after flipping flag, I see immediate drop in 429-rate by ~70% in the canary slice (CloudMetrics). Charts: `rate/429` for eu-west-1 canary down from 18/min to 5/min within 60s.
jordan: confirming in logs that exemption mapping fallback is back to legacy behavior. We probably reverted to old code path.
maya: good observation — can we confirm token accounting didn't double-charge anyone? Need quick audit.
jordan: quick check: token-ledger write counts show small window (10:02-10:04Z) where some requests were marked as non-exempt and incremented usage. I'll run a reconciliation query.
ashley: searching for `token_accounting_diff` shows ~1200 affected requests across 6 tenants. Most requests were short; estimated billable tokens ~18k.
priya: is that within SLA tolerances? Customers might see brief rate-limits.
support-lead: already pushed a short customer blurb: "We experienced a brief error in rate limiting for some requests after a canary rollout. We rolled back the canary and services have stabilized. We're investigating impact and will follow up." Sent to priority customers.
maya: have we fully rolled the canary back or only flipped flag? We need to ensure no auto-rollouts continue.
jordan: canary controller shows the canary slice stopped progressing and traffic rerouted to previous variant at 10:06Z. Canary pods are terminating. Canary deployment status: `stable: false`, `rolled_back: true`.
incident-bot: Postmortem draft created: https://wiki.redwood/INC-33421/postmortem — assign owner: jordan.
devin: support asks if we can proactively credit affected tenants — what's the rough token delta and policy?
ashley: rough delta per dedicated tenant: 2-5k tokens; enterprise customers: 3-6k. I recommend a quick audit job to generate a CSV of affected requests.
jordan: already queued `reconcile-tokens` job with query window 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z to 2026-03-15T10:06:00Z. Job id: recon-20260315-01.
maya: assigning follow-ups: - jordan: own postmortem + reconciliation run - ashley: validate token ledger integrity and confirm whether double decrement happened - priya: prepare incident timeline + alert rule adjustments - devin/support: customer comms and credits plan
priya: any indication this hit Dedicated Reserved capacity throttles and triggered evictions?
ashley: no pod evictions. Only application-level 429s. No infra scaling events.
support-lead: customers are asking for RCA ETA. I'd like a short explainer: cause = canary change to exemptions mapping omitted legacy grandfathering for some tenant tags -> resulted in over-throttle for those tenant tokens -> mitigated by flipping flag + canary rollback.
jordan: will publish detailed timeline + code diff in postmortem. Root cause: config merge missed a guard clause for `tenant_type: reserved` when migrating exemption lists.
maya: closing incident if metrics stable for next 30m. Leaving bridge open for reconcilers.
incident-bot: Severity lowered to P2 at 10:28Z based on stabilization.
ashley: recon job completed — CSV result uploaded to S3: `s3://incidents/33421/recon-20260315-01.csv` (contains account, request_ts, tokens_charged).
jordan: prepared patch to add guard and unit tests, PR: https://github.com/redwood/rlv3/pull/8421 — will schedule for controlled deploy after review and canary plan.
devin: customers OK with interim credit approach. We'll coordinate billing credit once reconverged.
maya: final notes: lessons — add canary smoke test for exemptions mapping against reserved/dedicated tenant matrix, add alert that correlates 429 spikes with `tokens_alloc`==0 for known-exempt accounts.
priya: agreed. I'll add the monitoring tickets and link to postmortem.
support-lead: thanks everyone — I'll keep customers updated with the postmortem link when available. :thumbsup:
jordan: thanks — will take owner for follow-ups.
maya: incident thread closed for active mitigation; leave timeline comments in postmortem.
